title: Progressive fair-share smoothing + local fallbacks for limiter degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We have observed two recurring operational pain points during cross-region bursts and limiter-side outages: 1) aggressive cold rejecting of requests from clients that previously had steady traffic (unfairness), and 2) wide blast radius when the global limiter goes into degraded mode (large percentage of tokens rejected across regions).

Goal: Implement a progressive fair-share smoothing algorithm combined with tiny per-region "local reservoirs" and staged fallback admission policies so that: (a) short spikes are absorbed without permanent token loss for healthy tenants, (b) traffic is smoothed fairly across users and regions during contention, and (c) during limiter process outages we degrade customers gracefully with per-tenant prioritized soft-credits and an ordered circuit-breaker that prefers local fallbacks before global reject.

Scope: server-side admission + quota enforcement changes in the limiter service (limiter-fleet), small coordination protocol for cross-region state seeds, runtime knobs for smoothing windows and reservoir sizes, updated console metrics and runbook. No API surface changes for customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New smoothing preserves 99th percentile latency SLOs for low-latency customers under steady-state; 2) In a synthetic multi-region spike test (see test harness link), at least 70% of short bursts (<30s) are absorbed by local reservoirs without global token consumption; 3) Fairness: per-tenant short-term allocation deviation reduced by >=40% versus baseline during mixed-traffic tests; 4) During a controlled limiter leader outage, the staged fallback reduces global request rejects by >=50% compared to immediate global fail-open/fail-closed baselines; 5) Automated canary + rollout steps pass and related dashboards surface the new metrics (reservoir_hit_rate, smoothing_backpressure, staged_rejects).
implementation_plan:
Phase A (spike 1-2 wks): prototype smoothing algorithm in limiter dev branch; expose config for smoothing_window_ms, smoothing_alpha, reservoir_capacity_pct; instrument metrics.
Phase B (2-3 wks): implement per-region tiny reservoirs seeded from recent token deltas and a simple positive-only reconciliation window to limit cross-region chatter; add staged fallback levels: (0) normal admission, (1) local reservoir drain, (2) soft-credit priority for high-SLA tenants, (3) global shedding by weight.
Phase C (1 wk): integrate circuit-breaker hooks to trigger staged fallback on limiter leadership loss or degraded RT percentiles; add unit/integration tests and chaos test scenarios.
Phase D (1 wk): rollout canary to dev region then two commercial regions, monitor metrics and abort criteria, update runbook.

Engineering notes: Keep the admission path fast and lock-free where possible. Use atomic token counters per-tenant and per-region. Reservoir reconciliation will be eventual and conservative (no negative credit transfers). Avoid adding synchronous cross-region RPCs on the hot path.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated behind runtime flag limiter.smoothing.enabled.
2) Canary: 5% traffic in dev region for 24h. Abort on metric regression (>5% increase in 99p latency or >2x increase in errors).
3) Ramp to 25% across dev+staging regions for 48h.
4) Pilot in 2 production regions with non-critical tenants for 72h.
5) Full roll after 7-day stability window and sign-off from SRE/PM.
6) Emergency rollback: disable flag and immediately return to existing admission policy.

Make sure runbook has clear diagnostics to distinguish local reservoir exhaustion vs global shedding.
monitoring_and_alerting:
New metrics to add: limiter.smoothing.window_ms, limiter.reservoir.capacity_pct, limiter.reservoir.drain_rate, limiter.reservoir_hit_rate, limiter.staged_fallback_level, limiter.per_tenant_deviation_pct.
Create dashboards: "Smoothing Health", "Reservoir Utilization by Region", and "Staged Fallbacks by Tenant Tier".
Alerts: P1 alert when reservoir_hit_rate < 0.1 for >2m in a region concurrently with increased 5xx errors; P2 when staged_fallback_level >= 2 for >5m across >1 region.
SLO implications: update quota-enforcement SLO doc to reflect that short bursts are absorbed by reservoirs and should not count as token rejections for incident classification.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Added complexity could introduce regressions or edge-case starvation for low-volume tenants. Mitigation: conservative default reservoir_capacity_pct (e.g., 3-5%), long smoothing windows for first rollout, automated fairness tests in CI.
Risk: Cross-region divergence if reconciliation fails. Mitigation: design reconciliation as best-effort; rely on global periodic checkpoints; ensure fallback to global shedding if reconciliation is too stale.
Risk: Observability blind spots. Mitigation: ship metrics with feature and require green dashboards in canary prior to ramp.
